ownerDecision.functionalConsent: Owner explicitly authorizes additive development and counter-review without an additional external human reviewer.
ownerDecision.provenanceRule: Do not characterize machine self-review or second user-controlled GitHub login as an independent human security approval.

summary: Only actual authenticated MCP ToolExtra with OAuth mcp:write and existing GovernedSessionService lookup can mint a proof.
One-use 32-byte random browser-entered proof, scoped by exact server/parent/label/documentRoot, expires after at most 180 seconds.
Server checks web-cookie signature, signed E3 target/session, same origin and exact FQDN before invoking pairing redemption.
Server verifies OAuth principal/client/expiry and live MCP transport binding again when redeeming the proof.
One-use pairing state is process-local with bounded capacity; broker caches the bearer encrypted under a process-local AES-256-GCM key and discards it on consume/expiry.
Existing B3f runtime reader is called with server-authenticated MCP transport, never a browser-supplied ID, principal, claim or lock.
Existing Plesk SSH executor and E3 issuer retained; no parallel task/session/lock authority introduced.
Original router behavior remains compatible for legacy tests when requireMcpPairing is unset.

findingsClosedAtCodeLevel: Browser cannot assert or forge transportSessionId through the Plesk form.
Browser proof cannot be replayed or carried to a different server, parent, label or document root.
Expired proof, expired OAuth token and unbound governed session fail closed.
Compromised or invalid pairing proof produces a generic failure with no bearer or E3 secret echoed.
No privileged operation is executed by the new MCP pairing tool; OAuth mcp:write is required to issue it.
Past 7 review findings retain regression tests and a separate 8th historical comment regression.
limitationsAndOpenRisks: The web dashboard uses a shared-secret signed cookie, not an individually verified user principal; the bearer pairing proves MCP session possession but cannot claim a universal human identity guarantee.
Process-local pairing state is not multi-worker; a worker restart or cross-host pairing fails closed rather than transferring authority.
Even encrypted transient bearer storage remains sensitive to full process-memory compromise; no plaintext bearer is written to disk or audit records.
The B3f runtime admission module still explicitly returns runtimeWriteAuthorized:false even if all read-only proofs are observed.
Existing B3d durable single-use signed E3 receipt is not installed into a production write-admission path. A pairing proof is NOT an E3 atomic consumption receipt.
No actual Plesk subscription/admin permissions for the target server and domain have been observed by an authorized write-capable provider.
Existing GitHub review/CI release policy requires evidence that has not been obtained. Owner's waiver cannot be labeled an independent GitHub APPROVED.
Current MCP bridge write-context is project-scoped, with free_shell:false, run_command_s1:false, run_command_s2:false, and no generic Plesk create-subdomain tool.
The existing server and Plesk write command remain unmodified in production because PR #355 is not merged or deployed.
